name: volume_breakout_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus
thesis: A volume breakout occurs when volume on a single bar exceeds 5x its 20-bar SMA AND price simultaneously breaks to a new session high/low. The extreme volume signals that a large participant (institution, algo) is aggressively entering the market. Unlike price-only breakouts (which fail ~60% of the time), volume-confirmed breakouts have a higher success rate (~55%) because the volume demonstrates real capital commitment. The edge exists because most breakout traders use fixed volume thresholds (e.g., >2x average), while using a 5x threshold is much more selective and catches only the most extreme volume events. The inefficiency persists because the 5x threshold is so strict that it filters out most breakout attempts, leaving only genuine institutional-participation events.
mechanism: Consolidation periods accumulate resting orders above resistance and below support. A breakout triggers these resting orders as stop-losses and breakout entries fire simultaneously. The resulting order flow imbalance overwhelms the resting liquidity, and market makers widen spreads in the breakout direction, accelerating the move.

conditions: high > session_high[t-1] (new session high on the vol spike bar)
(close - low) / (high - low) > 0.7 (closed near high of bar)
low < session_low[t-1] (new session low on the vol spike bar)
(high - close) / (high - low) > 0.7 (closed near low of bar)

exit.signal_exit: exit if a reverse vol spike >3x occurs in opposite direction

filters.volume_filter: 5x is the core filter — extremely strict, by design

weaknesses: 5x volume spikes are rare — may see 0-2 qualifying signals per day across the entire NIFTY 200 universe
Some 5x volume spikes are caused by block deals or basket trades at market midpoint — no directional information
The confirmation bar requirement means entering after a large-volume bar, where slippage may be higher than normal 3 bps
prior_art: Volume breakout is a core concept in TA (Edwards & Magee, 'Technical Analysis of Stock Trends'). Volume precedes price is a market adage attributed to Joseph Granville. Using extreme volume thresholds (5x) is less common than the standard 2x threshold in literature. Related to the 'uptick volume' concept from the NYSE TICK indicator.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
